newsitem.title: USA: Clinton wants NATO expanded, dialogue with China.
newsitem.headline: Clinton wants NATO expanded, dialogue with China.

text.p: President Bill Clinton vowed on Tuesday to go to China to pursue a deeper dialogue with Beijing and said he wanted to see NATO expanded by 1999 to include former communist states in Central Europe.
In remarks prepared for delivery in his State of the Union address to Congress and the nation, Clinton said America's first task is to help build an undivided, democratic Europe.
"To that end, we must expand NATO by 1999, so that countries that were once our adversaries can become our allies," he said.

A NATO summit in Madrid in July to due to name the first former communist Central European states it aims to admit in 1999. Russia strongly opposes NATO enlargement but has agreed to enter talks on closer ties with the 16-nation Western alliance. On that score, Clinton said, "We must build a stable partnership between NATO and a democratic Russia."

The president said the United States also "must pursue a deeper dialogue with China" because working with China, instead of isolating it, is the best way to work out differences. He and Chinese President Jiang Zemin have pledged to make reciprocal visits.

"I will go to China and I have invited China's president to come here, not because we agree on everything, but because engaging China is the best way to work on common challenges like ending nuclear testing -- and to deal frankly with fundamental differences like human rights," he said.
